Entering Beirut — site analysis

plot 1,488.5 m² survey BOURJ HAMMOUD.dwg date —
Base The map is the professor’s cadastral survey (BOURJ HAMMOUD.dwg) — georeferenced by identifying its coordinate system as EPSG:22780 (Deir ez Zor / Syria Lambert) and cropped to 580 × 496 m around the plot, because the drawing covers far more of Bourj Hammoud than this project needs. Parcel boundaries, surveyed structure lines, easements, encroached walls, dividing lines, parcel numbers, and the survey’s own street names. No other map is drawn as base geometry. What sits on top of it is the analysis — businesses, arrival points, greenery, wind — plotted as annotation, and every mark names where it came from when you click it. Structures are drawn as lines and never filled: that layer is wall linework, not closed footprints (only 2 of its 941 entries close, and the median entry’s two ends are 7.6 m apart), so filling it invents shapes that do not follow the walls. The project plot is the polygon the professor drew and X-ed on layer 0 of the same file: 1,488.5 m² against the brief’s 1,500 m². Still open is its parcel number — it is a carve-out of parcel 2478 and has none of its own.

Sources
  • BOURJ HAMMOUD.dwg — the professor’s official cadastral survey. Converted DWG→DXF headlessly with AutoCAD 2027 accoreconsole.exe, read with ezdxf, transformed EPSG:22780→WGS84 with pyproj, parcel faces rebuilt with shapely.ops.polygonize.
  • Solar geometry computed for 33.90° N. Everything else on these drawings is measured off the survey itself.
